articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz v Flavio Cobolli: ATP Finals tennis group stage – live
articles.summary: ATP Finals updates from the afternoon action in Turin Mail Katy | Kartal’s fightback against injury and abuse. And talking about Agassi: this is a lovely trip down memory lane of the 1990 season-ending final. Buongiorno!
body: Buongiorno! With Carlos Alcaraz already guaranteed to finish top of the Ivan Lendl group after two straight-sets wins, the biggest jeopardy going into his match against the already-eliminated Flavio Cobolli is the state of his left hamstring. After picking up the injury against Daniil Medvedev on Wednesday, Alcaraz had an MRI scan yesterday and was cleared to play on, so now we’ll get to see if he can still hit the absurd levels he did earlier this week.

While Alcaraz is riding a late-season wave after his wrist injury-enforced summer hiatus, sweeping up titles in Tokyo, Vienna and Paris, Cobolli was reduced to tears after the 7-6, 6-0 loss to Frances Tiafoe that sealed his exit two days ago. The Italian – the only home player in the Jannik Sinner-less singles – said it was the saddest match of his career and that he felt he’d let the Turin crowd down on his ATP Finals debut. But Cobolli still described today’s meeting with Alcaraz – just the second of his career – as “a beautiful gift … I hope to annoy him as much as possible, even if it won’t be easy”.

body: Spain will face France in the Nations League quarter-finals in a rematch of their World Cup semi-final. England will play Norway in another World Cup rematch, but another matchup between Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappé was the standout prospect from the Nations League draw made Friday.

Spain beat France 2-0 in July on its way to a World Cup title. England beat Norway 2-1 in the quarter-finals. The other quarterfinal pairings Friday were the Netherlands against title holder Portugal and Belgium against Germany.

The winners advance to the Final Four mini tournament from 9-13 June to be hosted by one of the teams. The host should be decided on 7 December at Uefa’s executive committee meeting in Belfast, Northern Ireland.

These quarter-finals have been set a high bar by the previous edition in March 2025. Then, three of the four quarterfinals went to extra time in the second leg — two to penalty shootouts — and included 3-3 draws between Spain and the Netherlands and Germany against Italy, when the Italians trailed 3-0 at halftime. Portugal advanced to the Final Four by beating Denmark 5-2 after extra time in the second leg.

articles.title: Scotland change captain again as Darge injured
articles.summary: Scotland are forced into a late change for Saturday's Nations Championship visit by Japan after Rory Darge, who was due to captain the side, is ruled out through injury.
body: Scotland have been forced into a late change for Saturday's Nations Championship visit of Japan after Rory Darge, who was due to captain the side, was ruled out through injury.

The Glasgow Warriors forward had been carrying a shoulder injury from last weekend's win over Australia and, following further assessment and discussion within the Scotland camp, it has been decided he will sit out the game at Murrayfield.

Club-mate Matt Fagerson will start instead at number eight, with his place on the bench filled by Edinburgh flanker Freddy Douglas and Newcastle Red Bulls' Ollie Leatherbarrow moving forward in the back row.
Head coach Gregor Townsend had already made 10 changes for Japan's visit with several top players, including fly-half Finn Russell, rested.

articles.title: How the Columbus Crew switched paths en route to the MLS playoffs
articles.summary: In a transformative year, Crew GM Issa Tall’s boldest change may have been to abandon his best-laid plans. The Columbus Crew have a more holistic operation than most in MLS. The club as a whole still exists thanks to the dogged efforts of their fervent fanbase that helped block relocation.
body: And yet, this year tested the conventions set by team and league alike.

In January, chief soccer officer Issa Tall welcomed the club’s eighth head coach, Henrik Rydström. Having only previously coached in his native Sweden, the 50-year-old used his introductory presser to laud the values of relationism, to praise his predecessor, and to plot a bold course for a new Crew. It was assumed he’d be around a while – the Crew have historically been patient with coaches, needing only seven bosses to navigate their first 30 seasons.

By mid-May, after just 16 games in charge, Rydström was on his way back to Sweden. His five wins were the lowest of the eight full-time Crew coaches. And yet, Saturday sees the Crew begin the MLS Cup Playoffs in a best-of-three matchup with Lionel Messi and Inter Miami.

articles.title: Bukayo Saka may not return for Arsenal before Christmas, Mikel Arteta admits
articles.summary: Zubimendi also out of Saturday’s game at Newcastle. Arteta imposes Fantasy Premier League ban after leak. Mikel Arteta has said Bukayo Saka may not return before Christmas as the Arsenal forward continues his rehabilitation from a thigh injury.
body: Saka has been out since limping off against Bayern Munich at the end of last month, and it is understood he has yet to resume light training. Arteta revealed more tests during the international break confirmed the England forward did not need surgery and that he was expected to be out for another four weeks.

When asked whether Saka could be fit for the game against Manchester United on 20 December, Arteta was unsure. “I cannot be that specific,” he said. “In four weeks’ time a lot of things can happen. Maybe it is three and then it is five.

“At the end, there are a few elements. One is the healing of that tissue – and we cannot predict exactly when that tissue is going to be in the best condition to push it. Then there is the rehab plan that we have now, what he needs to do in the gym, what he needs to do in terms of treatment and on the field.”

articles.title: Stoke and Birmingham proving you shouldn't judge a book by its cover
articles.summary: Stoke host Birmingham in a Championship game of two teams both bang in form going into the latest international break. How will they re-emerge?
body: That is a "tale of two cities" that did not look too likely to get written when Mark Robins' Potters started this season with three straight defeats and Blues won only two of their first eight league games under Chris Davies.
But, just like you should never judge a book by its cover, the footballing equivalent is to never judge any league table until after 10 games.
The season is now three months old - after Saturday's meeting at the Bet365 Stadium it will be more than a third of the way in.
And a clearer picture is starting to emerge as to whether what was once the "worst of times", especially in Stoke's case, might yet become the "best of times" before this 46-game campaign ends.

articles.title: Cummins retains Cricket Australia support as captain
articles.summary: Pat Cummins will retain backing from Cricket Australia to remain as Test captain despite ongoing and explosive allegations about the sandpaper controversy.
body: A detailed testimony from Cameron Bancroft supported previous claims made by Usman Khawaja that the entire Australia team – including Cummins – knew of the plan to tamper with the ball during a Test match against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018.
Cummins has always denied involvement in or knowledge of the cheating plot, and reiterated his stance in a 68-minute address to the media last week.
CA has regularly spoken of its support for Cummins, and the fast bowler will be allowed to continue in the captaincy role he has held since 2021. A statement could be issued over the weekend.
Cummins, 33, is due to lead Australia in the first Test against New Zealand on 9 December. A squad for the series opener against the Black Caps has not yet been named.

articles.title: Guimaraes growing at Arsenal - but Arteta still wants more
articles.summary: It's all eyes on Bruno Guimaraes this Saturday. The Newcastle hero who captained the team to cup success returns in Arsenal colours. And he returns as a growing cog in the Gunners' system.
body: Despite being Newcastle's key man, the Brazilian endured a slow start to life at Arsenal. An early-season injury did not help, nor did the early-season form of Myles Lewis-Skelly in the Brazilian's absence.
But now he is back in the North East as a first-choice option, having impressed in Arsenal's recent league wins over Liverpool and Hull, while also scoring crucial goals against Sunderland and Leeds.
"He's still not there," said Arteta after the 1-0 win over Hull last time out. "He's much better, he's hitting serious levels now, but we can still take the player to another level."
The comments were a surprise, given Guimaraes had just received a standing ovation from the Arsenal crowd as he was substituted following an impressive display.

articles.summary: Puka Nacua is given a three-game suspension for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy, although the Los Angeles Rams wide receiver was already out injured.
body: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua has been given a three-game suspension by the NFL for violating the league's personal conduct policy.
In March, the 25-year-old was sued for assault and battery by a woman who says he made an antisemitic statement and bit her on the shoulder on New Year's Eve.
Nacua's attorney has denied any statement was made and described the bite as "horseplay".
That incident came two weeks after Nacua performed an antisemitic gesture during a livestream appearance, for which he later apologised.

articles.title: Drone operator takes down Man Utd footage and issues apology
articles.summary: The drone operator who posted footage of Mauricio Pochettino's first training session at Manchester United on YouTube has said he has now removed the video.
body: The 12-minute drone footage over United's Carrington training ground showed the the Argentine overseeing various tactical drills with his new team as they prepared for their game against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

CC Overview, who posted the footage, said on Friday morning: "I would like to speak about yesterday's incident. A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part. My aim was to picture Mauricio Pochettino in his United training kit for the supporters to see for the first time.
"I had wrongly presumed that with it being close to the start of the session that no meaningful training sessions would have started so would have been some harmless warming up shown.

"I also wrongly assumed that the training session would have been open to various media outlets. I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.

articles.title: Erasmus running risk of breaching World Rugby ban with watchalong
articles.summary: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus would risk breaching the terms of his six-Test ban if he holds his planned online watchalong of Saturday's Nations Championship clash with Ireland, Sky Sports understands.
body: Erasmus is serving a six-match suspension handed down by World Rugby following extraordinary claims, saying "match-fixing" and "manipulation" was occurring in rugby after his side's defeat to France in Paris last week.

"The suspension applies with immediate effect, applies to international matches, and includes any matchday involvement including coaching, direct or indirect contact with team management or players on matchdays; entering the stadium, coaches' box, playing enclosure, technical area, approaching and/or communicating with match officials on matchday; engaging in any 'feedback' process with match officials; and engaging in media duties during the suspension."

Regarding the "direct or indirect contact with team management or players on matchdays" element of his suspension, Sky Sports sought guidance on the potential for one of South Africa's coaching staff or management set-up signing up and listening to and watching the reactions and comments of their suspended head coach during Saturday's contest - something which could have a bearing on prospective replacements and tactics in the Test.

articles.title: How does Euro 2028 qualifying work? Confirmed pots, format, and rules for co-hosts
articles.summary: England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland will co-host the tournament as the qualifying draw takes place in Belfast on Sunday December 6
body: Co-hosted on home soil by England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland, the road to Euro 2028 is fast approaching as the draw for qualifying takes place in Belfast in early December.
But the four co-hosts will enter qualifying for the tournament as normal, even though there is a ‘safety net’ that can be used by two of the teams should they fail to qualify automatically.
The United Kingdom hosted some games during the Covid-delayed Euro 2020 tournament in 2021, although many matches were played with limited capacities due to Covid restrictions.
Wembley hosted the final and will do so again in 2028, with Cardiff, Glasgow, Dublin, Birmingham, Liverpool, Manchester, Newcastle also staging games during the 24-team tournament.

articles.title: Khawaja branded 'biggest traitor ever' in Sandpapergate fallout
articles.summary: Former South Africa bowler Fanie de Villiers has branded Usman Khawaja "the biggest traitor he's ever seen" after the ex-Australia batter's allegations about the Sandpapergate affair.
body: Khawaja said in his autobiography that every member of the Australia team was aware of the plot to manipulate the ball with sandpaper on the 2018 South Africa tour, a claim backed up by David Warner, Chadd Sayers and, most explosively, Cameron Bancroft.

Bancroft - who, along with Warner and then-captain Steve Smith, served a ban following the rumbling of the ball-tampering plot - wrote in a 4,000-word-plus article in the West Australian newspaper that Pat Cummins' vehement denials made him break his silence.
Current Australia Test skipper Cummins stated in a 68-minute press conference last week that Khawaja's claims were "utter nonsense", which Bancroft said left him feeling "angry, betrayed and alone".
De Villiers, who played 18 Tests and 83 ODIs for South Africa between 1992 and 1998 told Perth's 91.3 SportFM, that Khawaja had "broken every single code of conduct".
